Hi all,

I'm posting this because the police warning about fake tablets is buried on here and I don't think enough people have read it. Please read it properly, then share it. Don't just like it.

The police say blue tablets are being sold as diazepam or "Xanax". Some of them contain nitazenes, which are synthetic opioids and can be far stronger than heroin. A tablet that looks like the real thing can stop someone breathing. Signs to watch for: extreme drowsiness, pinpoint pupils, slow or noisy breathing, and blue lips. The police have said their priority is preserving life, and that's what this is about.

If someone you're with is getting worse, ring 999 straight away. Don't wait. Don't put them to bed to sleep it off, and don't wait to see if they come round. Someone who has taken an opioid can stop breathing, and the brain can go without oxygen very quickly. Hours is far too long. If they're drowsy and you can't wake them properly, that's an emergency. And don't worry about getting in trouble for calling. The only thing that matters is getting help there in time.

Naloxone nasal spray reverses opioid overdose. It's free from the Brightpath drug and alcohol service on Stockport Road, next to the launderette. They're open Monday to Friday 10 till 4, and Thursdays till 7. Anyone can ask, you don't need to give a name, and the training takes about 10 minutes. Get it before you need it. It doesn't replace calling 999, so ring anyway.

For parents: please talk to your kids this week, not after half term or whenever it comes up. I had the conversation with my 14-year-old over his tea last night. He rolled his eyes, but he listened, and he asked me what pinpoint pupils meant. Keep it short and direct. Tell them what the tablets look like, what to do if a mate is unwell, and that you'd rather get a call at 3am than anything worse. Tell them they can ring you no matter what has happened.

For everyone else: the thread about Saturday night is full of rumours and people having a go at the kids involved. I get that people are upset, but it doesn't help anyone. Scared kids don't ring for help, and that's exactly how this gets worse. Stop guessing about who was involved. If you know something useful, pass it to the police.

Please share this with your friends, your kids' group chats, and anyone with teenagers. Thank you.

Becky
